14_esgo_position_screening.titleEn: European Society of Gynaecological Oncology/European Network of Gynaecological Advocacy Groups Position on risk-based cervical cancer screening
14_esgo_position_screening.abstractEn: The ESGO 2026 position statement recommends replacing cytology with HPV DNA testing as the primary screening method for cervical cancer to provide stronger protection; advocates gender-neutral HPV vaccination to accelerate herd immunity, especially where coverage has not reached WHO targets; suggests HPV genotyping combined with age and screening history for individualized risk assessment; and considers that methylation testing may significantly reduce unnecessary colposcopy referrals in a fully molecular screening model.
14_esgo_position_screening.excerptEn: The Risk-Based Screening for Cervical Cancer project was a 4-year Horizon 2020 European research consortium that developed and validated a risk-stratified approach to cervical cancer screening, moving away from the current one-size-fits-all model. The European Society of Gynecological Oncology and its network advocate for risk-based screening strategies.

2_ec_methylation_consensus2026.titleEn: Expert Consensus on Clinical Application of Gene Methylation Screening Technology for Endometrial Cancer (2026 Edition)
2_ec_methylation_consensus2026.abstractEn: The Expert Consensus on Clinical Application of Gene Methylation Screening Technology for Endometrial Cancer (2026 Edition) was developed by multiple societies and multidisciplinary experts through several rounds of consensus meetings. In response to the rising incidence of endometrial cancer in China and the challenging prevention and control situation, the consensus addresses gene methylation testing technologies approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), describing screening workflows, risk assessment, and management strategies for symptomatic, increased-risk, and high-risk populations, with recommendations aimed at standardizing clinical application and improving early detection, early diagnosis, and early treatment.
2_ec_methylation_consensus2026.excerptEn: To further standardize the clinical application of gene methylation testing technology in endometrial cancer screening in China, improve the level of early detection, early diagnosis, and early treatment of endometrial cancer, and promote precise prevention and standardized management of endometrial cancer in China, this expert consensus was developed under the leadership of the Chinese Society of Gynecologic Oncology, the Obstetrics and Gynecology Committee of the Chinese Research Hospital Association, and the Women's Health Medicine Branch of the China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care, jointly with multidisciplinary experts in gynecologic oncology, obstetrics and gynecology, pathology, and tumor epidemiology through multiple rounds of consensus meetings. As the incidence of endometrial cancer in China continues to rise with a trend toward younger patients, the prevention and control situation is increasingly severe. Endometrial cancer has well-defined high-risk factors, making precise identification of high-risk populations and rational application of novel screening technologies particularly critical. Gene methylation testing technology has now received national approval.

1_methylation_tech_spec.titleEn: Technical Specification for Tumor DNA Methylation Biomarker Detection
1_methylation_tech_spec.publisherEn: Group Standard (China Association for Laboratory Testing)
1_methylation_tech_spec.abstractEn: This technical specification (2026), published by the China Association for Laboratory Testing, specifies the testing requirements and quality control for tumor DNA methylation biomarker detection, clarifying key process steps and quality indicators. It applies to medical institutions and testing laboratories conducting tumor DNA methylation biomarker detection, providing a unified technical basis for the standardized application of methylation testing in tumor screening and auxiliary diagnosis, and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of test results.
1_methylation_tech_spec.excerptEn: This document specifies the testing requirements and quality control for tumor DNA methylation biomarker detection. This document applies to medical institutions and testing laboratories conducting tumor DNA methylation biomarker detection.

4_cfdna_methylation_consensus2025.titleEn: Expert Consensus on Laboratory Testing and Clinical Application of Circulating Cell-Free DNA Methylation Tumor Markers (2025 Edition)
4_cfdna_methylation_consensus2025.abstractEn: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation testing, as a non-invasive liquid biopsy technology, has significant value in tumor early screening, auxiliary diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and recurrence warning. This consensus, organized by the Laboratory Medicine Branch of the Chinese Medical Association, systematically standardizes the laboratory testing workflow (specimen collection and preservation, methodology selection and performance validation, result interpretation and reporting standards) and quality control requirements for circulating cell-free DNA methylation tumor markers, aiming to promote the standardized application of cfDNA methylation testing and provide reliable technical support for precision tumor diagnosis and treatment.
4_cfdna_methylation_consensus2025.excerptEn: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation testing, as a non-invasive liquid biopsy technology, demonstrates significant value in tumor early screening, auxiliary diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and recurrence warning. This consensus, organized by the Laboratory Medicine Branch of the Chinese Medical Association, systematically standardizes the laboratory testing workflow, quality control, result interpretation, and clinical application scenarios for circulating cell-free DNA methylation tumor markers, covering pre-test specimen collection and preservation, mid-test methodology selection and performance validation, and post-test result interpretation and reporting standards, aiming to promote the standardized and normalized application of cfDNA methylation testing and provide reliable technical support for precision tumor diagnosis and treatment in clinical practice.

12_cervical_screening_guide2.titleEn: Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening (II)
12_cervical_screening_guide2.publisherEn: Chinese Journal of Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology
12_cervical_screening_guide2.abstractEn: The Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening (II) (2025) were developed by experts from seven Chinese societies/associations, focusing on standardizing the triage of abnormal cervical cancer screening results to avoid over-diagnosis and missed diagnosis through refined management. For HR-HPV primary screening positive results, cervical cytology is the main triage method; for cytology primary screening positive results, management is stratified by risk. p16/Ki-67 dual staining, methylation testing, and HPV genome integration testing can be used for triage in relevant populations, and the reagents used must be recognized by authoritative institutions and clinically validated.
12_cervical_screening_guide2.excerptEn: Considering the incidence of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical cancer in China and global cervical cancer screening strategies, and to achieve the goal of eliminating cervical cancer, experts from seven Chinese societies/associations jointly developed the Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening (II). These guidelines focus on standardizing the triage methods for abnormal cervical cancer screening results, aiming to avoid over-diagnosis and missed diagnosis through refined management. For HR-HPV primary screening positive populations, cervical cytology is the main triage method; for cervical cytology primary screening positive populations, management is based on the risk level of their results. In addition, p16/Ki-67 dual staining can be used for triage of HR-HPV primary screening without genotyping or positive results for the other 12 HR-HPV types (excluding HPV 16/18).

13_molecular_testing_consensus.titleEn: Chinese Expert Consensus on Molecular Testing Technologies for Cervical Cancer Screening and Early Diagnosis (2025 Edition)
13_molecular_testing_consensus.publisherEn: Chinese Journal of Health Care and Medicine
13_molecular_testing_consensus.abstractEn: Cervical cancer is the most significant reproductive system malignancy threatening women's health. The Chinese Expert Consensus on Molecular Testing Technologies for Cervical Cancer Screening and Early Diagnosis (2025 Edition), based on the current status of cervical cancer screening and advances in molecular testing technologies, systematically summarizes the role of molecular testing technologies such as HPV testing and DNA methylation testing in cervical cancer screening and early diagnosis, standardizes the clinical application of these technologies, and provides strong support for cervical cancer screening and early diagnosis.
13_molecular_testing_consensus.excerptEn: Cervical cancer is the most significant reproductive system malignancy threatening women's health. With the continuous development of molecular biology technologies, molecular testing technologies such as human papillomavirus testing and DNA methylation testing play increasingly important roles in cervical cancer screening and early diagnosis. This consensus, based on the current status of cervical cancer screening and advances in molecular testing technologies, summarizes molecular testing technologies related to cervical cancer screening and diagnosis, standardizes their application in cervical cancer screening, and provides strong support for cervical cancer screening and early diagnosis.

9_pax1jam3_consensus.titleEn: Expert Consensus on the Workflow, Reporting, and Clinical Application of PAX1/JAM3 Dual-Gene Methylation Testing for Cervical Cancer
9_pax1jam3_consensus.abstractEn: This consensus (2025), developed by the Laboratory Medicine Professional Committee of the Chinese Association of Integrative Medicine in collaboration with multiple societies/associations and multidisciplinary experts in laboratory medicine, pathology, and obstetrics and gynecology, comprehensively reviews the laboratory workflow, quality control standards, and specimen collection and processing for PAX1/JAM3 dual-gene methylation testing for cervical cancer, and provides recommendations on testing reports and clinical application, aiming to promote the standardized application of cervical cancer methylation testing in laboratory and clinical settings and ensure accurate and reliable test results.
9_pax1jam3_consensus.excerptEn: Based on the current status of cervical cancer screening and the development of screening methods and strategies, the Laboratory Medicine Professional Committee of the Chinese Association of Integrative Medicine, jointly with multiple societies/associations, organized laboratory, pathology, and obstetrics-gynecology multidisciplinary experts to develop this consensus on methylation testing and clinical application. The consensus comprehensively reviews the laboratory workflow, quality control standards, specimen collection and processing for PAX1/JAM3 dual-gene methylation testing, and proposes recommendations on the significance and function of PAX1m/JAM3m testing, laboratory testing workflow, quality control, testing reports, and clinical application. The consensus aims to promote the standardized application of cervical cancer methylation testing in laboratory and clinical settings, ensure the accuracy and reliability of test results, and provide practical and forward-looking guidance for clarifying clinical application scenarios.

3_ec_prevention_consensus2025.titleEn: Chinese Expert Consensus on Three-Tier Prevention Strategies for Endometrial Cancer (2025 Edition)
3_ec_prevention_consensus2025.publisherEn: Chinese Journal of Practical Gynecology and Obstetrics
3_ec_prevention_consensus2025.abstractEn: Endometrial cancer is one of the most common gynecologic malignancies worldwide. Affected by population aging, increasing metabolic diseases, and changing fertility patterns, its incidence continues to rise, and in some cities it has become the most common malignancy of the female reproductive tract. The Chinese Expert Consensus on Three-Tier Prevention Strategies for Endometrial Cancer (2025 Edition) proposes promoting primary prevention, secondary prevention (early screening and diagnosis), and tertiary prevention (comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation) through multidisciplinary collaboration, to reduce disease risk and improve survival rates and quality of life.
3_ec_prevention_consensus2025.excerptEn: Endometrial cancer (EC) is one of the most common gynecologic malignancies worldwide. Due to population aging, the rising prevalence of metabolic diseases, and changes in fertility patterns, its incidence continues to increase. In developed countries and some Chinese cities such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, endometrial cancer incidence has become the most common malignancy of the female reproductive tract. Effective prevention and management of endometrial cancer requires multidisciplinary collaboration, encompassing primary prevention, secondary prevention, and tertiary prevention strategies.

2_dna_methylation_consensus2024.titleEn: Expert Consensus on Detection and Clinical Application of Tumor DNA Methylation Biomarkers (2024 Edition)
2_dna_methylation_consensus2024.publisherEn: Chinese Journal of Cancer Prevention and Treatment
2_dna_methylation_consensus2024.abstractEn: The Expert Consensus on Detection and Clinical Application of Tumor DNA Methylation Biomarkers (2024 Edition) points out that DNA methylation biomarkers are increasingly important in cancer diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. The consensus provides a series of recommendations on the definition, clinical significance, testing standards, and data processing of methylation biomarkers, as well as their application in tumor screening, auxiliary diagnosis, companion diagnosis, and recurrence monitoring, aiming to enhance the understanding of clinical and laboratory professionals, standardize testing workflows, and promote their application throughout the tumor diagnosis and treatment process.
2_dna_methylation_consensus2024.excerptEn: With the development of biomedicine, methylation biomarkers are increasingly important in cancer diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. This expert consensus aims to comprehensively review the testing technologies, clinical applications, and potential of DNA methylation biomarkers in tumor management. In addition, the consensus provides a series of recommendations on the definition, clinical significance, testing standards, data processing, and application of methylation biomarkers in tumor screening, auxiliary diagnosis, companion diagnosis, and recurrence monitoring, based on the latest research progress and practical clinical experience, aiming to enhance the understanding of clinical and laboratory professionals, standardize testing workflows, and promote their application throughout the tumor diagnosis and treatment process, thereby providing patients with more precise and effective treatment options.

3_cervical_screening_guide1.titleEn: Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening (I)
3_cervical_screening_guide1.publisherEn: Chinese Journal of Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology
3_cervical_screening_guide1.abstractEn: The Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening (I) (2023) were developed by experts from seven Chinese societies/associations, recommending high-risk HPV nucleic acid testing as the primary screening method for cervical cancer, cytology for regions without HPV nucleic acid testing capacity, and co-testing for resource-sufficient regions, opportunistic screening populations, and special populations. Age 25 is the starting age for screening; women aged 25-64 should undergo HPV testing alone or co-testing every 5 years, or cytology every 3 years; women over 65 with adequate prior negative screening may discontinue screening.
3_cervical_screening_guide1.excerptEn: Considering the incidence of cervical intraepithelial lesions and cervical cancer in China, as well as global screening strategies, and to achieve the goal of eliminating cervical cancer, experts from seven Chinese societies/associations jointly developed the Chinese Guidelines for Cervical Cancer Screening. These guidelines recommend high-risk HPV nucleic acid testing as the primary screening method for cervical cancer, using HPV nucleic acid testing methods and reagents recognized by authoritative domestic and international institutions and clinically validated for primary screening. Cervical cytology screening is used in regions without HPV nucleic acid testing capacity, and when conditions mature, screening methods based on HPV nucleic acid testing are adopted. Co-testing is used for cervical cancer screening in resource-sufficient regions, opportunistic screening populations, and certain special populations. Age 25 is the starting age for screening; women aged 25-64 should undergo HPV nucleic acid testing alone/co-testing every 5 years, or cytology every 3 years. Women over 65 with adequate prior negative screening may discontinue screening.
